packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-16 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this packet was in my context. The only external labels I saw are the modern pencil shelfmark notes written on the parchment itself (visible as "Stams, STA, Frg. 75-1r", "...75-1v", and "...75-2r"/"...75-2v" on the strip). They give a shelfmark, not a text identification.
- Beyond the brief: the left strip on face A is mounted upside down, so I made 180-degree rotated copies of image-002, -003, -004, -007, -008, -009 in my session scratchpad (sips -r 180) to read them. Line numbers marked "rot" count from the top of the ROTATED view, which is the bottom of the stored file. I also ran `ls` on the packet directory and read image sizes with sips. I opened nothing else and did not read packet.json.
- I did not consult any edition or search. Much of the text is liturgical/scriptural. Where letters were clear I wrote the words out, but familiarity with common Latin may have shaped some expansions. Anything I was unsure of is marked with ?.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
Two faces (overviews image-001 and image-017), each showing two separate pieces of parchment:

FACE A (overview image-001; tiles 002-016, 5 x 3 grid):
 (a) LEFT: a horizontal strip of about 15 lines, mounted UPSIDE DOWN. It has one column of
     text cut at both sides. There are red rubrics, red-touched capitals and red punctuation.
     Superscript corrections ("dei", "deus") are added with red carets. One rubric line is
     underlined in red, and the last lines carry Arabic numerals ("folio 1?1"). Pencil
     shelfmark "...Frg. 75-2r" is in the margin.
 (b) RIGHT: a larger leaf, upright, single column, about 34 lines. The bottom left is torn away
     diagonally, and the lower left edge has a row of sewing/stitch holes. The top margin is
     cropped close. There are red one-line initials and red strokes on capitals. Short chant
     incipits are underlined in red, with red abbreviations for chant genres ("off", "co",
     "Alla", "v"). Red rubrics (one line looks like a heading, possibly naming a gospel)
     separate the sections. Near the bottom, a red-ruled line is followed by short black
     lines with ARABIC NUMERALS ("132" in red, "178"), small superscript numbers ("63", "21",
     "2?"), then a red rubric and a new reading. There are wormholes and losses near the
     bottom right. Pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 75-1r" is at the foot.
FACE B (overview image-017; tiles 018-029, 4 x 3 grid):
 (a) LEFT: the same strip, now upright: 16 lines, one column, cut at both sides and at top and
     bottom. It has red initials, red rubrics ("Ep(isto)la b(ea)ti pauli ap(osto)li ...",
     "S(e)c(un)d(u)m math..."), red-underlined headings and a red marginal number at the left.
 (b) RIGHT: the dorse of the larger leaf, which is BLANK. Only show-through, stains, holes and
     the pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 75-1v" are visible (tiles 021, 025, 029).
Tiles 012, 013, 014, 026, 027 and parts of 028 show only the black cloth and the colour chart.

Tentative interpretation (not certain): service-book texts in a sequence of prayer (collect)
-> chant incipits -> rubric -> reading (epistle/prophecy) -> rubric -> gospel. Main text only.
I saw no commentary or glosses beyond the corrections.

Selected spans: I read almost everything legible on the strip (both faces) and on the large
leaf. Unread or weak areas: the top line of the strip on both faces (cut or abraded), the
damaged middle of face-B line 1-3, several lines in the middle of the large leaf where the
ink is faded, and the bottom block of the large leaf (lines with numerals, plus damage).

======================================================================
